scenes.headline: How a network learns without backprop's illegal moves
scenes.sub: Error Diffusion in a dual-stream network that obeys Dale's principle
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cannoli! Real neurons are either excitatory or inhibitory, never both. This paper trains a network that obeys that rule, without backpropagation.

scenes.text: Don't carry the error back through transposed weights. Broadcast the output error straight to every hidden unit, and update each layer locally.
scenes.mark: Broadcast the output error straight to every hidden unit
scenes.say: Standard backprop needs each synapse to know its partner's weight. Error Diffusion instead broadcasts the output error straight to every hidden unit.

steps.say: Each layer carries two streams: an excitatory vector p and an inhibitory vector n.
Within-stream weights feed forward, and every learnable weight is constrained non-negative.

steps.note: the minus sign is wired in, not learned
steps.say: The cross-stream terms are subtracted, and that minus sign is hard-wired, not learned. So Dale's principle holds by construction.
A signed output just subtracts the two streams.

scenes.title: Routing the blame
scenes.text: R = S M^T,  r(i) = i mod C

parts.note: output error S, broadcast by a fixed routing matrix M
parts.say: The output error is broadcast through a fixed routing matrix. No transposed weights, nothing random.

parts.note: hidden unit i takes class channel i mod C
parts.say: Hidden unit i takes the error of output channel i mod C, wrapping around the classes.

parts.note: each layer scales R by its local slope, then updates
parts.say: Each layer scales that drive by its own activation slope, and updates from local activity alone.

scenes.title: Three fixes that make it learn
scenes.say: Out of the box, it scores just fifty point four percent on MNIST. Three fixes close the gap.

items.say: Wider sigmoids keep the slope alive in early layers, against a twenty-five-fold decay.
Centering each class's error over the batch removes a constant bias.
And the network starts excitation-heavy, about three to one.

scenes.title: MNIST test accuracy, author-reported
scenes.say: The result: ninety-six point seven percent on MNIST, sixty-one point seven on CIFAR-10. Near a backprop-free baseline, short of backprop.

scenes.text: Networks can learn under the brain's wiring rules, and which fix carries them depends on the task.

recap: Excitatory and inhibitory streams, non-negative weights
Output error broadcast to every layer, by modulo
Which fix matters most depends on the task
scenes.say: To recap: two signed streams, blame broadcast instead of carried back, and a bottleneck that moves with the task.
